theorem_title: Raw prefix query equals independent bucket mass
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.RawPrefixCounts.prefixQuery_eq_bucketPrefixMass {h J : ℕ} (P d : ℤ)
    (A : Finset α) (B : Finset β) (C : Finset γ)
    (a : α → ℤ) (b : β → ℤ) (c : γ → ℤ) (w : _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.RawReporting.Wanted h J α)
    (k : ℕ) (pre : List (Finset (Fin (464 * h)))) :
    _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.RawReporting.prefixQuery (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.RawIncidences.rawOn h J P d (A ×ˢ (B ×ˢ C)) a b c) w k pre =
      _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.RawPrefixCounts.bucketPrefixMass P d A B C a b c w k pre := by sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $h,J,k\in\mathbb N$, $P,\delta\in\mathbb Z$, finite index sets $A,B,C$ over finite decidable types, integer maps $a,b,c$, a wanted label $w$, and a list $u$ of local subset prefixes be arbitrary. For the raw incidences on $A\times B\times C$,

$$\operatorname{prefixQuery}(\operatorname{rawOn}(A\times B\times C),w,k,u)=\operatorname{bucketPrefixMass}(P,\delta,A,B,C,a,b,c,w,k,u).$$

This identifies the abstract reporting query with the independently trimmed physical source histograms.
